title: 1967 AHSME Problem 34
statement: Points \(D,\) \(E,\) \(F\) are taken respectively on sides \(AB,\) \(BC,\) and \(CA\) of triangle \(ABC\) so that \(AD:DB=1:n,\) \(BE:CE=1:n,\) and \(CF:FA=1:n.\) The ratio of the area of triangle \(DEF\) to that of triangle \(ABC\) is:

solutions.text:
At each vertex, the two adjacent side fractions used by the corner triangle are \(\frac{1}{n+1}\) and \(\frac{n}{n+1}.\) Thus each corner triangle has area \(\frac{n}{(n+1)^2}\) times \([ABC].\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{[DEF]}{[ABC]} &=1-\frac{3n}{(n+1)^2}\\ &=\frac{n^2-n+1}{(n+1)^2}. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Subtract the three corner triangles from triangle \(ABC\)
Each corner triangle has area ratio \(\frac{n}{(n+1)^2}\)
